item.title: Appi Kogen Resort: Tohoku's Powder & Highland Playground — Guide
item.description: Appi Kogen is one of Tohoku’s largest ski resorts — famed for long, well-groomed runs of light powder snow in winter, drawing skiers from across Japan and abroad. In summer the highland turns green for golf, hiking and family activities, making it a year-round mountain playground in northern Iwate. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Hachimantai, Iwate Hours Winter ski season; summer activities Admission Lift passes / activity fees vary Time needed Half–full day Best time Winter (powder); summer (highland) What to Do Long, groomed powder-snow ski runs in winter.

item.title: Hachimantai & Yakehashiri Lava: Iwate's Volcanic Highland — Guide
item.description: Hachimantai is a serene volcanic highland straddling the Iwate–Akita border — a plateau of alpine marshes, ponds and hot springs. It holds the rare Yakehashiri lava flow (a national natural monument) and the famous ‘Dragon Eye’, a ring-shaped snowmelt pattern that appears on a highland pond in late spring. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Hachimantai, Iwate Hours Aspite Line road ~Apr–Nov Admission Free Time needed Half day Best time Late May (Dragon Eye); summer alpine What to See The ‘Dragon Eye’ ring-shaped snowmelt pond (late May).

item.title: Mt. Odaigahara: Misty Highland Hiking — Nara Guide
item.description: Mount Odaigahara is one of Japan’s rainiest highlands, a plateau of misty forests, moorland and dramatic viewpoints deep in the Kii Mountains. Well-made boardwalk trails make its pristine nature accessible, with the popular East Course reachable by most walkers. 🗓️ At a Glance Location Kamikitayama, Nara Pref. Hours Daylight; road open ~late Apr–late Nov Admission Free Time needed 2–4 hours (East Course) Best time Summer greenery & autumn (Oct) What to See The East Course boardwalk loop past Hidegatake peak and Daijagura cliff viewpoint.
